q-44727.name: Question 1
q-44727.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x({x}^{2}y+2) & = \\ 3x({x}^{2}y)+3x(2) & = \\ 3\cdot {x}^{2+1}y+6x & = \\ 3{x}^{3}y+6x\end{aligned}
$$

q-110835.name: Question 2
q-110835.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{a}^{2}(2{a}^{4}-3{a}^{2}-6) & = \\ (-{a}^{2})(2{a}^{4})+(-{a}^{2})(-3{a}^{2})+(-{a}^{2})(-6) & = \\ ((-1)\cdot 2)({a}^{2}\cdot {a}^{4})+((-1)\cdot (-3))({a}^{2}\cdot {a}^{2})+((-1)\cdot (-6))({a}^{2}) & = \\ (-2){a}^{2+4}+(3){a}^{2+2}+(6){a}^{2} & = \\ -2{a}^{6}+3{a}^{4}+6{a}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-111117.name: Question 3
q-111117.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}(6-10{x}^{3}) & = \\ (\frac{x}{2})(6)+(\frac{x}{2})(-10{x}^{3}) & = \\ (\frac{1}{2}x)(6)+(\frac{1}{2}x)(-10{x}^{3}) & = \\ (\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6)x+(\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-10))(x\cdot {x}^{3}) & = \\ (3)x+(-5)({x}^{1+3}) & = \\ 3x-5{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

a

b

3x−5x4

Correct
EXPLANATION

We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

x2(6−10x3)=(x2)(6)+(x2)(−10x3)=(12x)(6)+(12x)(−10x3)=(12⋅6)x+(12⋅(−10))(x⋅x3)=(3)x+(−5)(x1+3)=3x−5x4
